title: Pilot jurisdiction selection (scored against explicit criteria) — gates M2–M6
context: Open-Spending-Explainers will publish plain-language, source-cited budget and contracts explainers for one pilot jurisdiction at a time. The pilot jurisdiction must be chosen before M1 content work begins because it fixes the source corpus, the source-reuse licensing reality, and the reviewer profile. Without a chosen jurisdiction, no budget or contracts source can be vetted, snapshotted, or ingested. The decision rule and deadline (2026-08-31) are fixed even though the specific jurisdiction is TO BE SECURED. This task is a hard gate on M2–M6.
objective: Research, score, and record the selection of the pilot jurisdiction against the five explicit criteria (open licensed data available, data quality/completeness, available public-finance reviewer, plausible distribution partner/audience, manageable accounting complexity), and either confirm the chosen jurisdiction or produce a shortlist with a fixed decision deadline of 2026-08-31.
acceptanceCriteria: Scores candidate jurisdictions against all five explicit criteria: (1) open/reuse-and-derivatives-licensed budget and OCDS contract data actually available and machine-readable; (2) data quality/completeness — reconcilable line items, documented fund structure; (3) an available credentialed public-finance reviewer for that jurisdiction; (4) a plausible distribution partner or audience (newsroom/library/open-data office/civic-tech org); (5) manageable accounting complexity for a first build

Records the decision — either a confirmed pilot jurisdiction with rationale, or a shortlist with the fixed decision deadline of 2026-08-31 — in a document that becomes the dependency artifact for M2–M6
Documents which jurisdictions were considered and why each was accepted or rejected against the criteria
Reviewed and signed off by the maintainer and noted for public-finance expert review once one is secured
output: A scored jurisdiction-selection document recording the pilot jurisdiction decision (or shortlist + decision deadline), candidate scoring against all five criteria, and the rationale — the artifact that M2–M6 source-vetting, ingestion, and content tasks depend on.
